{{short description|1=Spiral curve of the form r = a*sin(θ)/θ}}
[[File:Cochleoid with a=1.svg|thumb|upright=1.25|<math>r=\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}, -20<\theta<20</math>]]
[[File:Kochleoide als inverse zur quadratrix.svg|thumb|upright=1.25|cochleoid (solid) and its polar inverse (dashed)]]
[[File:Cochleoid.gif|thumb|upright=1.25|A flexible pole is fixed upright at one end and bent over to always form a circular arc. The other end then traces out a Cochleoid.]]

In [[geometry]], a '''cochleoid''' is a [[snail]]-shaped curve similar to a [[strophoid]] which can be represented by the [[polar equation]]
:<math>r=\frac{a \sin \theta}{\theta},</math>
the [[Cartesian equation]]
:<math>(x^2+y^2)\arctan\frac{y}{x}=ay,</math>
or the [[parametric equation]]s
:<math>x=\frac{a\sin t\cos t}{t}, \quad y=\frac{a\sin^2 t}{t}.</math>

The cochleoid is the [[inverse curve]] of [[Quadratrix of Hippias|Hippias' quadratrix]].<ref>Heinrich Wieleitner: ''Spezielle Ebene Kurven''. Göschen, Leipzig, 1908, pp. [https://archive.org/details/spezielleebenek01wielgoog/page/n277 256-259] (German)</ref>
